liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Not Fade Away** (3 reviews): Drums in Not Fade Away are played in an unusual way and lead beautifully into Eyes; Played at midnight, with an epic transition into Eyes Of The World [12][14][15]
- **Estimated Prophet** (2 reviews): The jam coming out of it is called killer, with odd vocals from Olatunji; Estimated Prophet into the jam is called fantastic; first set also praised [9][10]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Sugar Magnolia and Heaven's Door seen as a perfect ending to the New Year's Eve tradition [9]
- **Knockin’ On Heaven’s Door** (1 review): Closing song, played as a tribute to Bill, called good historical filler along with Sugar Magnolia [8]
- Vince Welnick has a strong night, notably in the impressive jam out of Terrapin [18]

## Setlist highlights

- **Midnight Madness**: rare: 7 archived performances [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1991-12-31.149663.sbd.cm.miller.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 180 min [1]
- **gd1991-12-31.sennME80.wklitz.94248.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 183 min; rated 3.75/5 by 4 [5]. Said about its sound: Very good audience recording of the show [18]
- **gd1991-12-31.sbd.ladner.tetzeli.fix-5921.76545.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 171 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [6]
- **gd91-12-31.sbd.ladner.5921.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 172 min; rated 3.47/5 by 15 [7]. Said about its sound: Phil's bass has a tone the reviewer loves and stands out, especially on Hell In A Bucket; Recording is full and wonderful, with prominent, powerful bass from Phil that drives the whole show [12][16]

## Around the show

- Described as the final New Year's show; the tradition closed with Sugar Magnolia and Knockin' On Heaven's Door, both dedicated to Bill [8]
- Before midnight, a montage of Bill Graham's countdowns played on the screen behind the stage [11]
- Called the band's last New Year's Eve show, with Jerry playing well [18]
- Babatunde Olatunji & Drums Of Passion and Bela Fleck & The Flecktones opened the show [1]
- Airto Moreira sat in on percussion for all of set 2 [1]
- Calls this the best Sugar Magnolia since Hornsby joined; notes many people dislike this New Year's show musically [10]
- Playing was just OK, falling short of the high standard expected for New Year's shows [11]
- Second set is less inspired than the previous year's show, which had Marsalis joining; band sounds choppy [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1991-12-31.149663.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  April 16, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [1]
- **gd1991-12-31.sennME80.wklitz.94248.flac16**: taped by Keith Litzenberger; transferred by Keith Litzenberger; source: Sennheiser ME-80's> Technics SV-MD1 (DAT) [5]
- **gd1991-12-31.sbd.ladner.tetzeli.fix-5921.76545.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Bill Tetzeli; source: Seamless edit of shnid 5921 [6]. Also: Fixed edit of the Ladner transfer: overlap between CDs 2 and 3 removed for seamless transition; converted from SHN to FLAC [6]
- **gd91-12-31.sbd.ladner.5921.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > Satellite Feed > DAT> CDR > WAV > SHNv3 [7]. Also: Soundboard via satellite feed to DAT, then CDR; transferred to SHN by C. Ladner from C. Larson's seed discs [7]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Oakland Coliseum Arena - December 30, 1991](https://www.dead.net/show/december-30-1991) [21]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Oakland Coliseum Arena - December 31, 1991](https://www.dead.net/show/december-31-1991) [22]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Oakland Coliseum Arena - December 30, 1991](https://www.dead.net/show/december-30-1991) [23]
